name: OpenAI Codex CLI
disclaimer: The reviewer's command - exec with its prompt, --model, -c model_reasoning_effort and options.trust_none - was run against codex-cli 0.160.0 on 2026-10-05; the rest is written from the documented interface and not verified against an install. Flags drift; correct and open a PR.

stdin.note: Verified from the command reference (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands, surface cli), read 2026-09-17: codex exec takes PROMPT as `string | - (read stdin)`, and `-` pipes the prompt from stdin.
Verified from the same reference: codex exec resume takes its PROMPT as `string | - (read stdin)` too.

options.trust_none_note: No flag removes codex exec's shell tool; its read-only sandbox leaves it reading. Measured on codex-cli 0.160.0, 2026-10-05: under --sandbox read-only, cat read a file, touch was refused (Operation not permitted) and curl resolved no host. Without --ignore-user-config the person's $CODEX_HOME/config.toml offered the model computer use, a browser and web search, and with it only the shell tool, waits and subagents. --ignore-rules leaves out the person's execpolicy rules, whose allow decisions approve commands without asking. ao runs a reviewer in a directory outside any repository, which codex exec refuses without --skip-git-repo-check, and --ephemeral keeps the review out of the person's sessions.

pin.note: codex exec runs read-only unless told otherwise, and a person's config.toml may set sandbox_mode; a reviewer names its sandbox, so no setting widens it.

mcp_isolation.why: MCP servers and plugins live in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml, which codex loads unless told not to (#24)

options.effort_note: The values the Responses API named when it refused another, through codex-cli 0.160.0 on 2026-10-05; each model takes a subset, listed in ~/.codex/models_cache.json.
options.sandbox_note: codex exec takes --sandbox and codex exec resume does not (openai/codex issue 40149); a resume takes -c sandbox_mode="<mode>", which every exec subcommand accepts.

--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandb.why: No documented combination runs an unattended implementer's loop without it. codex exec asks nobody - it answers every approval with never - and runs in a read-only sandbox unless told otherwise. Its workspace-write sandbox (-c sandbox_mode="workspace-write" after exec resume; --full-auto is gone since 0.147.0) keeps <writable_root>/.git read-only and the network off, so an implementer could edit and test but never stage, commit or run its reviewer. The watchdog starts no turn with it until a person names codex in watchdog.bypass_adapters on this machine, and ao doctor names what that allows. Read on 2026-09-17 from learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing, /docs/non-interactive-mode, /docs/developer-commands and /docs/config-file/config-reference, and github.com/openai/codex (codex-rs/exec/src/cli.rs; issues 40149 and 7071).
